title: First extragalactic detection of a phosphorus-bearing molecule with ALCHEMI: Phosphorus nitride (PN)
question: Search for P-bearing molecules outside the Milky Way towards the nearby starburst Galaxy NGC 253 and investigate the interstellar chemistry regulating their abundances.

data.arrays: ALMA main array and ACA (ALMA Compact Array)

what.value: Total H2 column density (N_H2) from dust continuum observations

evidence.loc: Detections of phosphorus nitride (PN) and LTE analysis
evidence.quote: We derived the relative abundance of PN compared to H$_{2}$, using the total column density of H$_{2}$, *N$_{\rm H_2}$*, derived by (cite: Mangum2019) from dust continuum observations with a similar spatial resolution than ALCHEMI (1.5$''\times$0.9$''$).

evidence.loc: Detections of phosphorus nitride (PN) and LTE analysis
evidence.quote: search for PN emission towards the Giant Molecular Clouds (GMCs) shown in Fig. 1 (we have adopted the labelling from (cite: Leroy2015)), with the exception of GMC 5.

what.value: Collisional data between PN and p-H2 from BASECOL

evidence.quote: We used the collisional data between PN and p-H$_2$ (cite: Najar2017PNData) taken from BASECOL (cite: Dubernet2013Basecol; Ba2020basecol) and prepared for RADEX with SPECTCOL.

what.value: Spectroscopic data from the CDMS and JPL catalogues

evidence.quote: Spectroscopic data obtained from the CDMS catalogue: PN entry 045511 (September 2019), PO entry 047507 (October 2019), PH$_{3}$ entry 034501 (May 2013), CP entry 043501 (March 2000), CCP entry 055503 (April 2009), $^{29}$SiO entry 045504 (January 2014), and C$^{34}$S entry 046501 (January 2004).
The spectroscopic data of PS was taken from the entry 63007 (January 1997) of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) catalogue.

what.value: Galactic PO/PN and PH3/PN ratios and PN, 29SiO, C34S column densities

evidence.loc: Correlation between PN and SiO abundances: Role of shocks
evidence.quote: Following this work, we show in Fig. 5 the column densities of PN and $^{29}$SiO, both normalised by the column density of C$^{34}$S, towards different Galactic sources detected previously.

external_data.citation: (cite: Rivilla2018; Rivilla2020; Rivilla2016; Bernal2021; Lefloch2016; Bergner2019)

recipe.goal: Inspect datacubes, extract spectra, and perform LTE line fitting and upper limit derivation
recipe.method: Extract spectra towards the continuum emission peak pixel of each GMC; generate simulated LTE spectra with MADCUBA-SLIM and fit with MADCUBA-AUTOFIT (or compute 3-sigma integrated intensity upper limits for non-detections); calculate abundances relative to H2 using N(H2) from Mangum et al. (2019).
key_parameters: FWHM fixed to 50 km s^-1 for PN and other P-bearing species
For GMC 4 and non-detections, Tex fixed to 4.4 K (derived from GMC 6)
assumptions: Beam filling factor of 1 (source size matches 1.6'' beam) and co-spatial distribution of species
PN and dust trace similar volumes of gas

recipe.goal: Perform non-LTE radiative transfer modelling of PN in GMC 6
recipe.method: Convert spectral intensities from Jy beam^-1 to brightness temperature (K) and model PN excitation and optical depth using SpectralRadex (RADEX LVG approximation) coupled with emcee MCMC sampling.
key_parameters: FWHM and v_LSR fixed to values from Table 2 (FWHM = 50 km s^-1, v_LSR = 184 km s^-1)
assumptions: Large velocity gradient (LVG) approximation and Gaussian spectral line profile
Channel uncertainties are independent, Gaussian, and 15% of the channel value

recipe.goal: Compare abundances and molecular ratios with Galactic sources and chemical models
recipe.method: Compare C34S-normalised PN and 29SiO column densities and PO/PN and PH3/PN upper limits against Galactic observations and the shock + cosmic-ray chemical models of Jiménez-Serra et al. (2018).
key_parameters: Shock model parameters: cosmic-ray ionisation rate zeta = 10^-13 s^-1, pre-shock density n(H) = 2x10^4 cm^-3
assumptions: C34S is optically thin and a good proxy for H2 barely affected by shocks or PDRs
All hydrogen is in molecular form, n(H) = 2 * n(H2)
